content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any ageing/transparency-related document(s) needed to identify the three allowed radiator candidates and their 10-year-equivalent humidity transparency losses. Record any numeric ageing losses and allowed thickness bounds relevant to each candidate."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard humidity requirement: exclude any candidate with transparency loss greater than 10%. From the remaining candidates, extract all material parameters or guidance in the documents that may affect pion/kaon separation, and decide the simulation scan grid over the allowed 1–6 cm thickness range."},{"id":"s3","description":"Run simulate_separation for each surviving radiator over the planned thickness grid across 1–6 cm, with enough points to identify the approximate optimum. Record all numeric separation results by radiator and thickness."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine the simulation near the best-performing thickness for the leading candidate(s), including neighboring thickness values within the allowed range, to determine the maximum pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c. Record the refined separation values."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare only candidates satisfying the ageing requirement, select the radiator and thickness with the highest simulated pion/kaon separation, and prepare the numeric evidence needed for the final recommendation, including rejected candidates and the reason for any hard-requirement rejection."}]}
